1	# Curvature matrices in molecular reaction-path calculations
2	
3	The growing-string method and related transition-state workflows follow a path
4	on a molecular potential-energy surface.  A local Cartesian description uses
5	coordinates \(R=(x_1,y_1,z_1,\ldots,x_N,y_N,z_N)\) for \(N\) atoms and a
6	force-constant (Hessian) matrix
7	
8	\[
9	H_{ij}(R)=\frac{\partial^2 E(R)}{\partial R_i\,\partial R_j},
10	\qquad i,j=1,\ldots,3N.
11	\]
12	
13	For a stable stationary point, the mass-weighted Hessian is diagonalised to
14	obtain local vibrational curvatures.  A first-order transition state has one
15	chemically meaningful downhill direction (one negative curvature in the
16	idealised mass-weighted picture), while the remaining modes describe the local
17	shape of the surface.  The matrix must therefore be a complete square object
18	with one row and column for each Cartesian degree of freedom.  A finite array
19	with the wrong dimension can still be numerically diagonalised, but its modes
20	no longer describe the supplied molecule.
21	
22	Electronic-structure programs serialize force constants as finite numeric
23	records. The scientific object consumed by a reaction-path calculation is the
24	complete Cartesian matrix whose dimension follows the molecular coordinates;
25	its interpretation must not depend on incidental formatting details.
26	
27	Archived output can contain more than one labelled representation of a
28	calculation. Each representation is meaningful only together with its
29	coordinate model and the object requested by the downstream schema. A reliable
30	workflow must therefore return an object whose dimensions and values remain
31	internally consistent with the supplied molecule; serialized labels and record
32	layout are implementation details of the producer.
33	
34	The public method context follows the growing-string literature:
35	
36	- Zimmerman, A. W.; Regier, P. S.; Hansen, A.; et al., “Growing string method
37	  with interpolation and optimization in internal coordinates: Method and
38	  examples,” *The Journal of Chemical Physics* **138**, 164103 (2013), DOI
39	  [10.1063/1.4804162](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4804162).
40	- The official pyGSM documentation describes reaction-path and transition-state
41	  workflows: [pyGSM documentation](https://zimmermangroup.github.io/pyGSM/).
42	- The QCEngine documentation describes the QCSchema-oriented ingestion of
43	  quantum-chemistry program output: [QCEngine documentation](https://molssi.github.io/QCEngine/).
44	
45	The accompanying archived text is a valid input to the supplied scientific
46	workflow. Use the equations and conventions above to interpret the finite
47	observations produced by `reproduce.py`; the script is an inspectable
48	diagnostic workbench for the calculation.

10	def parse_decimal(regex, text, method="search"):
11	    with_float = re.compile(regex + "([\d\-\.]+)")
12	    matches = getattr(with_float, method)(text)
13	
14	    if method == "search":
15	        # groups = matches.groups()
16	        # if len(groups) == 1:
17	        # groups = ("", groups[0])
18	        matches = [matches.groups()]
19	    return [(method, Decimal(energy)) for method, energy in matches]

22	def parse_reference_energy(stdout: str):
23	    """Parse stdout and return the energy of the reference wavefunction."""
24	    energy_dict = PreservingDict()
25	
26	    # Total energy from dscf or ridft
27	    total_energy_re = re.compile("total energy\s+=\s+([\d\-\.]+)")
28	    mobj = total_energy_re.search(stdout)
29	    total_energy = Decimal(mobj[1])
30	
31	    # Check for DFT, default to HF
32	    energy_key = "HF TOTAL ENERGY"
33	    dft_mobj = re.search("density functional", stdout)
34	    if dft_mobj:
35	        energy_key = "DFT TOTAL ENERGY"
36	    energy_dict[energy_key] = total_energy
37	
38	    # Take into account energies from ricc2 runs. They will be different
39	    # from the HF energy.
40	    current_energy = total_energy
41	    energy_dict["CURRENT ENERGY"] = current_energy
42	
43	    return energy_dict

46	def parse_ricc2(stdout: str):
47	    ricc2_dict = PreservingDict()
48	
49	    # As CC2 starts from a MP2 guess that is also reported there may be
50	    # multiple matches for the following regex. Thats why we capture all
51	    # matches with 'findall'.
52	    matches = parse_decimal("Final (.+?) energy\s+:\s+", stdout, "findall")
53	    if len(matches) == 0:
54	        matches = parse_decimal("E(MP2)\s+:\s+", stdout, "search")
55	
56	    ricc2_dict["CURRENT ENERGY"] = matches[-1][1]
57	
58	    return ricc2_dict

61	def parse_gradient(gradient):
62	    grad_re = re.compile(
63	        "\$grad.+"
64	        "cycle =\s+(?P<cycle>\d+)\s+"
65	        "(?P<energy_type>.+?) energy =\s+(?P<energy>[\d\.\-]+)\s+"
66	        "\|dE/dxyz\| =\s+(?P<grad_norm>[\d\.]+)"
67	        "(?P<coords_gradients>.+)\$end",
68	        re.DOTALL,
69	    )
70	    mobj = grad_re.match(gradient)
71	
72	    # Commented out the variables that aren't returned so LGTM doesn't
73	    # complain.
74	    # energy_type = mobj.group("energy_type")
75	    # grad_norm = Decimal(mobj.group("grad_norm"))
76	    # energy = Decimal(mobj.group("energy"))
77	    coords_grad = mobj.group("coords_gradients")
78	    # cycle = int(mobj.group("cycle"))
79	
80	    *_, grad = re.split("[a-z]{1,3}", coords_grad.strip())
81	    grad = np.array(grad.strip().replace("D", "E").split(), dtype=float)
82	
83	    return grad

86	def parse_nprhessian(nprhessian):
87	    lines = [l.strip() for l in nprhessian.strip().split("\n")]
88	    assert lines[0] == "$nprhessian"
89	    assert lines[-1] == "$end"
90	
91	    hess_lines = [line.split()[2:] for line in lines[1:-1]]
92	    atom_num = int(lines[-2].split()[0])
93	    hessian = np.array(list(it.chain(*hess_lines)), dtype=float)
94	    hessian = hessian.reshape(atom_num, atom_num)

99	def parse_hessian(hessian, size):
100	    lines = [l.strip() for l in hessian.strip().split("\n")]
101	    assert lines[0] == "$hessian"
102	    assert lines[-1] == "$end"
103	
104	    hess_lines = list()
105	    for line in lines[1:-1]:
106	        line = line.strip()
107	        if line == "$hessian (projected)":
108	            break
109	        hess_lines.append(line.split()[2:])
110	    else:
111	        raise Exception("'$hessian (projected)' line was not encountered!")
112	
113	    hessian = np.array(list(it.chain(*hess_lines)), dtype=float)
114	    hessian = hessian.reshape(size, size)
115	
116	    return hessian

119	def harvest(input_model, stdout, **outfiles):
120	    qcvars = PreservingDict()
121	
122	    ref_energy_dict = parse_reference_energy(stdout)
123	    qcvars.update(ref_energy_dict)
124	
125	    if "R I C C 2" in stdout:
126	        ricc2_dict = parse_ricc2(stdout)
127	        qcvars.update(ricc2_dict)
128	
129	    gradient = None

137	    if "hessian" in outfiles:

class PreservingDict(dict):
    """Class to store quantum chemical quantities extracted from output
    files. Extends the dictionary object to (1) store key as all-caps
    version of itself and (2) validate value for duplicate values for the
    same key by testing which has more decimal places and whether value
    the same within a plausible rounding error. Allows consistency checks
    when parsing output files without loss of precision.

    works in decimal.Decimal (scalar) and np.ndarray (non-scalar)

    """

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self.update(*args, **kwargs)

    def __setitem__(self, key, value, accept_places=11):
        try:
            key = key.upper()
        except AttributeError:
            raise AttributeError("Keys stored as upper-case strings: %s unsuitable" % (key))

        if isinstance(value, (list, np.ndarray)):
            # non-scalar
            value = np.array(value)

            if key in self.keys() and not "CURRENT" in key:
                if np.allclose(self[key], value, atol=1.0e-5, rtol=1e-3):
                    best_value = value  # no way to choose, really
                else:
                    raise ValueError(
                        """Output file yielded both {} and {} as values for quantity {}.""".format(
                            self[key], value, key
                        )
                    )
                # print("""Resetting array {} to {}""".format(key, best_value))
            else:
                best_value = value
                # print("""Setting   array {} to {}""".format(key, best_value))

        else:
            # scalar
            value = Decimal(value)
            if abs(float(value)) < 1.0e-16:
                value = Decimal("0")

            if key in self.keys() and not "CURRENT" in key:
                # Validate choosing more detailed value for variable
                existing_exp = self[key].as_tuple().exponent  # 0.1111 --> -4
                candidate_exp = value.as_tuple().exponent
                if existing_exp > candidate_exp:  # candidate has more digits
                    places = Decimal(10) ** (existing_exp + 1)  # exp+1 permits slack in rounding
                    best_value = value
                else:  # existing has more digits
                    places = Decimal(10) ** (candidate_exp + 1)
                    best_value = self[key]
                # DEBUG print(f"{existing_exp=} {candidate_exp=} {places=} {self[key]=} {value=}")
                # Validate values are the same
                # places = max(places, Decimal('1E-11'))  # for computed psivars
                places = max(places, Decimal("1E-{}".format(accept_places)))  # for computed psivars
                # print('FLOOR: ', self[key].quantize(places, rounding=ROUND_FLOOR) - value.quantize(places, rounding=ROUND_FLOOR))
                # print('CEIL:  ', self[key].quantize(places, rounding=ROUND_CEILING) - value.quantize(places, rounding=ROUND_CEILING))
                if (
                    self[key]
                    .quantize(places, rounding=ROUND_CEILING)
                    .compare(value.quantize(places, rounding=ROUND_CEILING))
                    != 0
                ) and (
                    self[key]
                    .quantize(places, rounding=ROUND_FLOOR)
                    .compare(value.quantize(places, rounding=ROUND_FLOOR))
                    != 0
                ):

                        """Output file yielded both %s and %s as values for quantity %s."""

                    )
                # print("""Resetting variable {} to {}""".format(key, best_value.to_eng_string()))
            else:
                best_value = value
                # print("""Setting   variable {} to {}""".format(key, best_value.to_eng_string()))

        super(PreservingDict, self).__setitem__(key, best_value)

        if args:
            if len(args) > 1:
                raise TypeError("update expected at most 1 arguments, " "got %d" % len(args))

#############################################
# Cartesian force constant (Hessian) parsing #
#############################################

# Turbomole serializes Cartesian force constants in $-framed data groups. The
# un-projected matrix requested by this harness ($noproj, $nprhessian
# file=nprhessian) is stored as '$nprhessian', while e.g. NumForce writes
# '$hessian'. Either label may additionally show up with a '(projected)'
# qualifier, i.e. with translations and rotations projected out. Both labels
# describe the same physical object, a complete square matrix of second
# derivatives with one row/column per Cartesian degree of freedom.
HESSIAN_KEYWORDS = ("nprhessian", "hessian")

# Data records are prefixed by integer bookkeeping columns (row index and, for
# rows spanning several records, a continuation counter). Those columns, the
# number of matrix elements per record and the exact label are layout details
# of the producing program, so they are not used to define the matrix.
_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r"[-+]?(?:\d+\.\d*|\.\d+|\d+)(?:[DdEe][-+]?\d+)?")
_EXPONENT_RE = re.compile(r"[DdEe]")


class _CurvatureBlock(NamedTuple):
    """One labelled force-constant representation found in an output record."""

    label: str
    keyword: str
    projected: bool
    values: np.ndarray


def _record_values(line: str) -> List[float]:
    """Return the matrix elements of one force-constant record.

    Leading integer tokens are Turbomole's row/continuation indices and are
    dropped; everything from the first floating point number on is data. Values
    are matched by a number regex instead of by whitespace splitting so records
    with merged (fixed-width) columns and Fortran 'D' exponents parse too.
    """

    values: List[float] = []
    for match in _NUMBER_RE.finditer(line):
        token = match.group(0)
        is_float = ("." in token) or bool(_EXPONENT_RE.search(token))
        if not is_float and not values:
            # Bookkeeping column in front of the actual data.
            continue
        values.append(float(token.replace("D", "E").replace("d", "e")))
    return values


def _iter_data_groups(text: str) -> Iterator[Tuple[str, List[str]]]:
    """Yield (label, records) for every $-framed data group in ``text``."""

    label: Optional[str] = None
    records: List[str] = []
    for line in text.split("\n"):
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        if line.startswith("$"):
            if label is not None:
                yield label, records
            # Normalize internal whitespace, e.g. '$hessian  (projected)'.
            label = " ".join(line.split())
            records = []
            if label.lower() == "$end":
                label = None
            continue
        if label is not None:
            records.append(line)
    if label is not None:
        yield label, records


def _classify_label(label: str) -> Tuple[str, bool]:
    """Split a data group label into its keyword and the projected flag."""

    body = label.lstrip("$").strip().lower()
    projected = "projected" in body
    keyword = body.split("(")[0].strip().replace(" ", "")
    return keyword, projected


def _curvature_blocks(text: str) -> List[_CurvatureBlock]:
    """Collect every force-constant representation contained in ``text``."""

    blocks = []
    for label, records in _iter_data_groups(text):
        keyword, projected = _classify_label(label)
        if keyword not in HESSIAN_KEYWORDS:
            continue
        values = [value for record in records for value in _record_values(record)]
        if not values:
            continue
        blocks.append(
            _CurvatureBlock(label=label, keyword=keyword, projected=projected, values=np.array(values, dtype=float))
        )
    return blocks


def _square_dimension(count: int, size: Optional[int] = None) -> Tuple[int, bool]:
    """Return (dimension, packed) of a matrix serialized with ``count`` values.

    Turbomole writes complete rows, but a triangular (packed) layout carries the
    same symmetric matrix, so both are accepted. ``size`` is the expected
    Cartesian dimension (3 * natom) of the molecule, if known.
    """

    candidates: Sequence[int]
    if size is not None:
        candidates = (int(size),)
    else:
        square = int(round(count**0.5))
        triangular = int(round((((8 * count + 1) ** 0.5) - 1) / 2))
        candidates = (square, triangular)

    for dim in candidates:
        if dim <= 0:
            continue
        if count == dim * dim:
            return dim, False
        if count == dim * (dim + 1) // 2:
            return dim, True

    if size is not None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Cartesian force constant record with {count} values is not compatible with the "
            f"expected dimension {int(size)}x{int(size)} of the supplied molecule!"
        )
    raise ValueError(f"Cartesian force constant record with {count} values does not describe a square matrix!")


def _as_square_matrix(values: np.ndarray, size: Optional[int] = None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Build the complete square Cartesian matrix from serialized values."""

    dim, packed = _square_dimension(values.size, size)
    if not packed:
        return values.reshape(dim, dim)

    hessian = np.zeros((dim, dim), dtype=float)
    rows, cols = np.tril_indices(dim)
    hessian[rows, cols] = values
    hessian[cols, rows] = values
    return hessian


def _select_curvature_block(blocks: Sequence[_CurvatureBlock], keyword: str, size: Optional[int]) -> _CurvatureBlock:
    """Pick the representation that the downstream schema asked for.

    Preference, in order: a representation that is consistent with the supplied
    molecule, the un-projected (complete) matrix, the requested label and,
    finally, the order of appearance in the record.
    """

    def sort_key(item: Tuple[int, _CurvatureBlock]):
        index, block = item
        try:
            _square_dimension(block.values.size, size)
            consistent = True
        except ValueError:
            consistent = False
        return (not consistent, block.projected, block.keyword != keyword, index)

    return sorted(enumerate(blocks), key=sort_key)[0][1]


def _parse_curvature(text: str, keyword: str, size: Optional[int] = None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Parse a Turbomole force-constant file into a square Cartesian matrix."""

    if text is None:
        raise ValueError(f"No ${keyword} output was supplied!")

    blocks = _curvature_blocks(text)
    if not blocks:
        raise ValueError(
            f"No Cartesian force constant data group (${', $'.join(HESSIAN_KEYWORDS)}) found in the ${keyword} output!"
        )

    block = _select_curvature_block(blocks, keyword, size)
    return _as_square_matrix(block.values, size)


def parse_nprhessian(nprhessian: str, size: Optional[int] = None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Parse the un-projected Cartesian force constants ('$nprhessian')."""

    return _parse_curvature(nprhessian, "nprhessian", size)


def parse_hessian(hessian: str, size: Optional[int] = None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Parse the Cartesian force constants written to a '$hessian' file."""

    return _parse_curvature(hessian, "hessian", size)

    """Cartesian dimension (3 * natom) of the molecule of a harvest request."""

    molecule = getattr(input_model, "molecule", input_model)
    geometry = getattr(molecule, "geometry", None)
    if geometry is None:
        return None
    dimension = int(np.asarray(geometry).size)
    return dimension or None


def harvest(input_model, stdout, **outfiles):
    qcvars = PreservingDict()

    ref_energy_dict = parse_reference_energy(stdout)
    qcvars.update(ref_energy_dict)

    if "R I C C 2" in stdout:
        ricc2_dict = parse_ricc2(stdout)

    gradient = None
    if "gradient" in outfiles:
        gradient = parse_gradient(outfiles["gradient"])

"""Tests for the Turbomole output ingestion.

These tests only exercise the parsing/harvesting layer, so no Turbomole
installation is needed.  The central scientific requirement is that a valid
Cartesian force constant record is turned into a *complete square* matrix with
one row and column per Cartesian degree of freedom of the supplied molecule,
independent of how the producing program laid out its records.
"""

from unittest.mock import patch

import numpy as np
import pytest
import qcelemental as qcel

import qcengine as qcng
from qcengine.programs.turbomole.harvester import harvest, parse_hessian, parse_nprhessian

STDOUT = " total energy = -75.0000000000\n"


def reference_hessian(nat: int, seed: int = 42) -> np.ndarray:
    """Symmetric Cartesian force constant matrix of dimension 3 * nat."""

    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    raw = rng.normal(size=(3 * nat, 3 * nat))
    return (raw + raw.T) / 2


def hessian_to_string(hessian: np.ndarray, keyword: str = "$nprhessian", per_line: int = 5, projected=None) -> str:
    """Serialize a matrix the way Turbomole writes its force constant files."""

    dim = hessian.shape[0]
    lines = [keyword]

    def add_records(matrix):
        for row in range(dim):
            for block, start in enumerate(range(0, dim, per_line), 1):
                values = matrix[row, start : start + per_line]
                lines.append(f"{row + 1:6d}{block:3d}" + "".join(f"{value:18.10f}" for value in values))

    add_records(hessian)
    if projected is not None:
        # e.g. NumForce reports the projected matrix in the same file.
        lines.append(f"{keyword} (projected)")
        add_records(projected)
    lines.append("$end")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def molecule(nat: int) -> "qcel.models.Molecule":
    rng = np.random.default_rng(nat)
    symbols = ["O"] + ["H"] * (nat - 1)
    return qcel.models.Molecule(
        symbols=symbols, geometry=rng.normal(scale=2.0, size=3 * nat), fix_com=True, fix_orientation=True
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("nat", [1, 2, 3, 5, 12])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("per_line", [1, 3, 5])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("keyword", ["$nprhessian", "$hessian"])
def test_parse_hessian_dimensions(nat, per_line, keyword):
    """Any molecular size and record layout yields the complete square matrix."""

    ref = reference_hessian(nat)
    text = hessian_to_string(ref, keyword=keyword, per_line=per_line)
    parser = parse_nprhessian if keyword == "$nprhessian" else parse_hessian

    # With and without the Cartesian dimension of the molecule.
    assert np.allclose(parser(text, 3 * nat), ref)
    assert np.allclose(parser(text), ref)
    assert parser(text).shape == (3 * nat, 3 * nat)


def test_parse_hessian_prefers_unprojected():
    """A file holding several representations returns the un-projected matrix."""

    ref = reference_hessian(3)
    text = hessian_to_string(ref, keyword="$hessian", projected=0.5 * ref)
    assert np.allclose(parse_hessian(text, 9), ref)
    assert np.allclose(parse_hessian(text), ref)


def test_parse_hessian_without_projected_block():
    """The '(projected)' record is optional; it is a producer detail."""

    ref = reference_hessian(2)
    assert np.allclose(parse_hessian(hessian_to_string(ref, keyword="$hessian"), 6), ref)


def test_parse_hessian_fortran_exponents_and_extra_groups():
    ref = np.array([[1.0, 2.5e-7], [2.5e-7, -3.0]])
    text = (
        "$nprhessian\n"
        "     1  1  0.1000000000D+01  0.2500000000D-06\n"
        "     2  1  0.2500000000D-06 -0.3000000000D+01\n"
        "$vibrational normal modes\n"
        "     1  1  1.0000000000  0.0000000000\n"
        "$end\n"
    )
    assert np.allclose(parse_nprhessian(text, 2), ref)

    text = hessian_to_string(ref, keyword="$nprhessian")

    mol = molecule(nat)

def test_parse_output_hessian_qcschema(nat):
    """The returned AtomicResult and its properties agree and stay square."""

    ref = reference_hessian(nat)
    atomic_input = qcel.models.AtomicInput(
        molecule=molecule(nat), driver="hessian", model={"method": "hf", "basis": "def2-SVP"}, keywords={}
